metaDescription: Six 1100-watt countertop microwaves compared on inverter power, sensors, grill and smart control, with honest picks for family kitchens.
expertTake: The Sharp SMC1464KS with inverter power is the best 1100-watt pick because it heats evenly at low settings where ordinary units pulse on and off. The Commercial Chef is the value choice for plain fast heating. Households that never defrost or cook beyond reheating can skip the extra features and buy the cheapest unit here.
introParagraphs: Microwaves in the 1100-watt class sit a step above the common midrange, which shortens cook times for family-sized portions. The extra power is helpful only if the cavity, tray and controls can use it well.

Beyond the headline number, the real differences are how the machine handles low-power cooking, how it senses doneness and how comfortable the panel is to use. This guide separates those traits so you pay for what you will actually use.

products.name: Sharp SMC1464KS 1.4 cu ft 1100W inverter microwave
products.description:
The SMC1464KS stands out because of its inverter circuit. A traditional microwave delivers lower power levels by switching the magnetron fully on and off, which is why a 30 percent defrost can leave edges cooked and centers frozen. An inverter keeps the output steady at the chosen level, and that makes thawing and gentle reheating noticeably more even.

It pairs that with a 1.4 cubic foot cavity, a 12.4 inch carousel tray and ten power levels with two-stage cooking. A gray interior and white LED display improve readability, and LED lighting helps you see food. Next to the non-inverter Sharp SMC1461KB, the same size and wattage, you pay for a different power delivery rather than extra space.

Ownership looks easy. Wipe the gray interior after spatter, wash the tray and keep the vents clear. Inverter boards add a component that a basic unit lacks, so use a surge strip if your power is flaky. For anyone who defrosts or simmers, this is the one to buy.
products.bestFor: People who defrost, melt and gently reheat often and want even results.
pros: Inverter output stays steady at low levels
1.4 cu ft cavity suits family portions
Two-stage cooking chains defrost and heat
LED lighting and display are easy to read
cons: Runs pricier than the non-inverter Sharp
Added electronics can be harder to repair

products.name: GE GCST14S1WBB 1.4 cu ft 1100W sensor microwave
products.description:
GE builds this around a moisture sensor that tracks steam so the oven ends the cycle when food is hot. For reheating a mixed plate or a bowl of soup, that removes the need to guess time. Seven convenience cook settings and one-touch start cover the familiar snack list.

A 1.4 cubic foot cavity with 1100 watts gives a balanced middle ground. It is not as roomy as the Farberware 1.6, yet it fits a dinner plate and heats it faster than the 1.1 cubic foot class. The black finish hides smudges better than stainless.

Wiping the interior after steamy foods keeps the sensor accurate, because a fogged cavity changes the reading. Expect the standard one year coverage and a panel that wants dry hands. If you want a recognized appliance maker and a sensor without the inverter price, this is a sensible pick. Against the Toshiba, you skip the voice features but keep a larger 1.4 cubic foot cavity, which many families will value more than an app.
products.bestFor: Households that want automatic reheating from a familiar appliance brand.
pros: Moisture sensor ends cooking when food is hot
1.4 cu ft with 1100 W is a balanced size
Black finish resists visible fingerprints
Seven presets with one-touch start
cons: No inverter, so low power pulses
Sensor accuracy drops in a steamy cavity

products.name: Toshiba 1.3 cu ft 1100W smart sensor microwave
products.description:
Toshiba adds smart connectivity to an 1100 watt sensor oven. With an Echo device you can start a preset by voice, and an app lets you send cook commands from your phone. It also carries sensor reheat, a mute function and a two-step child lock.

Voice control mostly helps with hands full of groceries, and the app is a convenience rather than a necessity. The 1.3 cubic foot cavity is a notch below the GE and Sharp 1.4 models. If you will not use the smart features, a simpler oven gives better value.

Smart units depend on home Wi-Fi, so an unreliable router can make the extras feel flaky, and the oven still works as a normal microwave when offline. Keep the door seal clean and update the app when prompted. It suits households already invested in a voice assistant, and the two-step child lock makes it a reasonable choice for homes with toddlers who like pressing buttons. Compared with the GE, you gain connectivity and lose a tenth of a cubic foot of room.
products.bestFor: Households already using Alexa who want hands-free start and a child lock.
pros: Alexa and app control add convenience
Sensor reheat takes guesswork away
Two-step child lock for family homes
Mute mode silences beeps
cons: 1.3 cu ft is smaller than the 1.4 units

products.name: Emerson MWG1191SB 1.1 cu ft 1100W microwave with grill
products.description:
Emerson is the only pick here with a built-in grill element. The grill browns and crisps the top of a dish, something plain microwaves cannot do, so toast, melted cheese and the top of a casserole improve. Eleven power levels sit alongside it.

At 1.1 cubic feet, it is smaller than the Sharp and GE. The grill element adds an extra heat source, so watch food and use heat-safe dishes. A rack would help if it is included, though you should confirm that against the listing. Against the Commercial Chef, you gain browning at a similar size.

The grill element collects grease, so wipe it once cool and never use the grill with plastic dishes. Run the grill alone for browning and use plain microwave mode for heating, because the two functions do different jobs and combining them without reading the manual can scorch food. It suits people without a toaster oven who want a little browning, and it keeps the 1100 watt speed for regular reheating when the grill is off.
products.bestFor: People who want crisping or browning from a single countertop unit.
pros: Built-in grill browns and crisps tops
Eleven power levels for fine control
Stainless cabinet with LED timer
1100 W output cooks quickly

products.name: Farberware 1.6 cu ft 1100W multi-stage microwave
products.description:
Farberware offers the largest cavity in this guide at 1.6 cubic feet while keeping 1100 watts. That extra volume helps with tall bowls, large dinner plates and casserole dishes. Ten power levels with multi-stage cooking give you full manual control over every cycle. Multi-stage means you can program a low-power thaw that rolls straight into a full-power heat, which is useful for a frozen lasagna slab that is too thick for one setting.

It does not have a sensor, so you set times yourself, and that is where the learning curve sits for new owners. Start with short bursts, stir, and add time, because a 1100 watt oven overshoots quickly when a portion is small. The larger body takes more counter space than the Commercial Chef, so measure first. Next to the GE at 1.4 cu ft, you gain headroom and lose automatic reheating.

Care is routine: wipe the interior, wash the tray and keep the back vents free. Because the cabinet is larger, the glass tray is also heavier and bulkier, so wash it carefully in the sink rather than wedging it into a crowded dishwasher. Best suited to cooks who often use wide dishes, and it pairs well with a household that cooks for four or more.
products.bestFor: Families that reheat large plates and casserole dishes.
pros: 1.6 cu ft cavity fits wide dishes
1100 W output speeds big portions
Multi-stage cooking chains steps
Stainless finish matches kitchens
cons: Large footprint on a small counter

products.name: Commercial Chef CHCM11100B 1.1 cu ft 1100W microwave
products.description:
Commercial Chef is the plain, fast 1100 watt oven in this lineup. It has touch controls with a digital LED display, ten power levels and a timer that runs from thirty seconds to 99 minutes. The unit weighs about 28 pounds, light enough to move.

There is no sensor, grill or smart feature. That keeps the price in the low tier and leaves less to break. A 1.1 cubic foot cavity fits a standard plate but not large dishes.

Keep the touch pad dry and the seal clean, since touch panels are the part that fails first on budget ovens when moisture creeps in. Choose it for buyers who just want speed, and next to the Farberware it saves counter space at the price of cavity room. Anyone who defrosts a lot should look at the inverter Sharp instead, because this oven pulses its power at low levels.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want 1100 watts and nothing extra.
pros: 1100 W at a low cost
Timer runs from 30 seconds to 99 minutes
Light enough to move around
Few features means few failure points

buyingCriteria.explanation: Compared with a 1000 watt oven, an 1100 watt unit trims cook time on a full plate by roughly ten percent. The gain is real but small, and cavity size and uniformity matter more. A 1.6 cu ft Farberware at 1100 W heats a big portion faster than the 1.1 cu ft Commercial Chef at the same wattage because there is room to space food.

A standard microwave runs low settings by cycling full power on and off, while an inverter holds a constant output. The Sharp SMC1464KS has it, and the Sharp SMC1461KB does not. If you defrost or melt chocolate, inverter power prevents cooked edges. For plain reheating at full power, the two behave alike.

Sensors on the GE and Toshiba measure steam to end the cycle automatically. They help with portions that change daily, but covered dishes and dry foods can fool them. A sensor adds cost, so skip it if you set times by habit.

The Emerson adds a grill that browns tops, which ordinary microwaves cannot do. The element also adds cleaning work and requires heat-safe dishes. Buy it only if you lack a toaster oven, since a dedicated oven browns better.

The Toshiba supports Alexa and phone control. These add convenience when your hands are full, but they depend on Wi-Fi and an app that may change. A smart oven without smart use is wasted money, so decide honestly whether you will use voice commands.

The Farberware at 1.6 cu ft is the roomiest, and the Commercial Chef at about 21 inches wide is among the leaner designs. Check turntable diameter, because 12.4 inches fits most plates. Leave space at the back for ventilation.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wattage match
howWeEvaluated.description: Only units with a stated 1100 W output were kept. Anything listed at 1000 W or 1200 W was removed. This keeps the comparison honest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power delivery
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated inverter ovens from pulse ovens using listed specs. The Sharp SMC1464KS stands alone with inverter power, while the SMC1461KB uses standard pulses. Defrost quality weighted this heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cooking aids
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted sensors, grill elements and smart control. The GE and Toshiba have sensors, the Emerson has a grill, and the Toshiba has voice control. Aids were credited only when useful.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cavity volume and outer dimensions from the sheets. The Farberware reaches 1.6 cu ft, while the Commercial Chef is about 21 inches wide. Tray width was weighted over volume.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership signals
howWeEvaluated.description: Reviews from owners gravitate toward touch pads and door latches as wear points. Simpler units earned reliability credit, and complicated smart models were checked for offline use.

cards.label: Inverter
cards.text: The Sharp SMC1464KS keeps output steady, so low-power defrost heats evenly. It suits people who thaw meat or melt butter often. It adds electronics that a basic oven lacks.

cards.label: Standard pulse
cards.text: The GE, Farberware, Emerson and Commercial Chef cycle the magnetron to hit low settings. Full-power reheating is unaffected. Defrosting can leave cooked edges.

howToChoose.note: Pick the Sharp if you defrost. Pick any other unit if you only reheat.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Family cooking needs a cavity that takes a wide plate, a sensor or staged cooking for varied portions, and a child lock if kids are around. A 1.4 cu ft cavity is usually enough.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GE offers a sensor at 1.4 cu ft, and the Toshiba adds a two-step child lock. The Sharp SMC1464KS is best if defrosting meat is a weekly habit.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You defrost often or want automatic reheating. The Sharp SMC1464KS and GE earn their cost through even heat and sensor cooking.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only warm drinks and leftovers. The Commercial Chef gives full 1100 W without paying for extras.

maintenance.why: Splatter bakes on and absorbs energy. A damp cloth while the walls are warm is easiest.
Grease smokes when heated. Dry it fully before placing it back on the hub.
Food film prevents a full close and can leak energy. Use mild soap and a soft cloth.
Grease on the Emerson element burns on next use. Let it cool before wiping.
Vents that get blocked trap heat and shorten magnetron life. Vacuum dust from slots.

faq.a: It cooks about ten percent faster on a full plate, which is helpful but not dramatic. Cavity size and features matter more. Choose by the other specs unless time is your top priority. Package directions usually assume a 1000 to 1200 watt oven, so an 1100 watt unit lands close to the printed time without adjustment, and a quick check at the minimum time is enough.

faq.q: Is an inverter microwave worth it?
faq.a: If you defrost meat or melt ingredients, yes, because power stays steady at low settings. For full-power reheating the difference is small. The Sharp SMC1464KS is the example here.
They help, but covered dishes and dry foods can confuse the sensor. Stir and rest food regardless. The GE and Toshiba are good at moist reheats.
They are handy with full hands, and the Toshiba still works as a normal microwave offline. Skip them if you will not use voice commands, since the cost is rarely justified otherwise.

faq.q: Can a grill microwave replace a toaster oven?
faq.a: Not fully. The Emerson browns tops, but it is slower and smaller than a toaster oven. It suits light browning.

faq.q: How long do these microwaves last?
faq.a: Owners can plan on several years, with the touch pad, door latch or magnetron as the usual failures. Clean seals and avoid running empty to extend life.
